social.text: Before I crack out the python-iron, does anyone know if there is a tool to automate getting layers from a Krita document into Blender as image layers? Kinda specific I know, but it would be super useful for 2.5d animation. I wrote a script* to import images and trace their alpha channels, but it relies on openCV for the image processing, and that doesn't natively open Krita documents. There are a few plugins that go the other way, that's not what I want. I want to be able to create a layered document in Krita, pull the lever and have them appear in a blend file as layers on planes. * https:// codeberg.org/stib/stibs_blende r_scripts/src/branch/main/import_and_trace_alpha.py # Krita # Blender # Python # AskFedi # OpenCV

social.text: "A metronome is a metronome." Not quite. Most are built on polling loops, and the drift shows up exactly where it hurts — fast tempos, odd subdivisions, the long session where you slowly stop trusting the click. Maestronom's core runs a deadline-armed scheduler: sub-millisecond accuracy, 30-300 BPM, tap tempo, 1-8 subdivisions, haptics on every beat.
